common_name: Francie L Camellia (Giant Rose-Pink Semi-Double Saluenensis-Reticulata Hybrid)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Francie L is a saluenensis x reticulata cross raised at San Marino's Huntington Gardens and prized for its huge, wavy-petaled rose-pink flowers.

directions: Francie L was raised from a cross of Camellia saluenensis and C. reticulata 'Buddha' made at the Huntington Botanical Gardens, with the seedling taking nearly two decades to reach its first bloom in 1960. Its very large, irregular semi-double flowers have wavy, loosely arranged rose-pink petals surrounding a prominent central boss of stamens, and the plant carries noticeably heavier, longer, dark green foliage than many reticulata hybrids. It forms an upright, slow-growing shrub that becomes a small tree with age and has proven more cold-tolerant than most pure reticulata selections. Grow it in humus-rich, acidic, well-drained soil in partial shade sheltered from harsh wind, feeding lightly and pruning only to shape right after flowering ends.

common_name: Pagoda Camellia (Songzilin, Historic Chinese Pine-Cone-Scale Reticulata Camellia)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Pagoda (Songzilin) is a historic nineteenth-century Yunnan cultivar whose overlapping, incurved petals resemble pine-cone scales.

directions: Pagoda, known in China as Songzilin and historically also traded under the name Robert Fortune, is one of the old Yunnan reticulata cultivars that reached Western collections in the nineteenth century. Its rose-red flowers are densely packed with narrow, overlapping incurved petals that stack in tiers reminiscent of a pine cone or a tiered pagoda roof, giving the bloom a tighter, more formal look than the loose peony-form flowers typical of many reticulata cultivars. The shrub is a steady, upright grower that eventually reaches small-tree size in a mild garden. Plant it in acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade with protection from drying winter wind, and limit pruning to shaping cuts made just after flowering.

common_name: Mouchang Camellia (Giant Salmon-Pink Semi-Double Reticulata Camellia)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Mouchang was raised in Escondido, California from a cross of two historic reticulata lines and bears extra-large salmon-pink semi-double blooms.

directions: Mouchang was bred in Escondido, California from a cross of the historic reticulata cultivars Chang's Temple and Mudan Cha, and its name honors that parentage. The semi-double flowers open extra-large and heavy, with broad salmon-pink petals and petaloids surrounding bright yellow stamens, on an upright, fairly open-growing shrub with large dark green leaves. It flowers in midseason and has been recognized with reticulata and hybrid awards from American camellia growers. Provide humus-rich, acidic, well-drained soil in partial shade sheltered from drying wind, and feed lightly after bloom while limiting pruning to shaping cuts made at that time.
